commentary_title: Handysize rates remain under pressure as tonnage increases across both basins
commentary_summary: The Handysize tonne-miles index edged down 5% to reach 116.2 in week 32, with rates continuing to move differently across both basins. Limited fresh enquiry and an increasing pool of vessel availability kept charterers in control, while the Atlantic saw further weakness in ECSA and softer activity in the US Gulf. The Continent and Mediterranean remained subdued, with only limited scrap and cement-related demand. The speed also slowed down across the east and the west. | The US Gulf faced the sharpest correction as a lack of new cargoes and a growing number of vessels weighed on fronthaul and transatlantic rates. The Continent also softened amid weaker Turkish scrap and fertiliser demand, while the East Mediterranean remained comparatively resilient, supported by new grain cargoes and stronger premiums for owners willing to trade via the Red Sea. | The Pacific lost some momentum as enquiries from North Asia eased and vessel availability increased across Southeast Asia and East Coast India. However, steady Chinese demand for Indonesian coal, continued South African cargoes in the Indian Ocean, and improving Australian export activity helped in limiting the further downside.
